title: Branches
subtitle: Every branch: how far it is from the default, merged or stale, protected, in a PR — rename, protect, clean up.
startBody: Its branches with last commit, open pull request and ahead / behind the default branch. Or switch to many repositories to create or protect branches everywhere at once.
truncated: This repository has more than 1,000 branches — only the newest 1,000 are shown.
none: No branches — the repository is empty.
aheadBehind: {{ahead}} commits ahead, {{behind}} behind the default branch
confirmDefault: Click again to make it the default

name.invalid: Not a valid branch name (no spaces, “..”, “~ ^ : ? * [ \”, or a leading / trailing “/” or “.”)
name.taken: A branch with this name exists

new.title: New branch
new.name: Name
new.fromHint: the new branch begins with this branch's latest commit

rename.title: Rename {{name}}
rename.note: A real rename: GitHub moves open pull requests and protection rules over, and links to the old name keep working.
rename.defaultNote: This is the default branch — it stays the default under the new name. Local copies need to switch to the new name.

protect.title: Protect {{name}}
protect.byPattern: Currently protected by the rule “{{rule}}”. Saving adds rules for this branch by name.

rules.noChecks: Add at least one check name

require_pr.name: Require a pull request
require_pr.what: Nobody pushes straight to the branch — changes come in through PRs.

dismiss_stale.name: New commits dismiss approvals
dismiss_stale.what: An approval only counts for what was reviewed.

code_owners.name: Require code owner review
code_owners.what: Files listed in CODEOWNERS need their owner's approval.

last_push_approval.name: Last push must be approved by someone else
last_push_approval.what: The person who pushed last can't approve their own change.

status_checks.name: Require status checks
status_checks.what: Listed checks (CI jobs) must pass before merging.

strict.name: Must be up to date
strict.what: The PR branch has to contain the latest changes of this branch.

conversation_resolution.name: Require resolved conversations
conversation_resolution.what: Every review comment thread must be resolved.

linear_history.name: Linear history
linear_history.what: No merge commits — squash or rebase only.

enforce_admins.name: Also for admins
enforce_admins.what: The rules apply to administrators too.

deletions.name: Deleting the branch
deletions.what: Anyone with write access could delete it.

many.fromHint: a branch name — empty = each repository's default branch
many.createNote: Goes through the queue: the dry run shows where the branch already exists or the source is missing.
many.protectNote: These rules go onto each repository's default branch (needs admin rights; private repositories need GitHub Pro / Team).
many.planNote: The dry run shows where rules are already identical or protection isn't available.

settings.staleDaysHint: A branch without a new commit for this long is marked stale.

rulesets.title: Rulesets
rulesets.intro: Rules GitHub enforces on branches — like protection, but for many branches at once and with a dry-run mode ("Evaluate"). Organization rulesets show here but are edited on the organization.
rulesets.name: Name

rule.pull_request: Require a pull request before merging

rulesets.checksPlaceholder: Check names, one per line (e.g. build, test)
rulesets.strict: Branch must be up to date first
rulesets.otherRules: Also has rules edited only on GitHub (kept unchanged): {{list}}
